messages:
sam: FYI — customer reporting a surge of 502/504s from /v1/rerank during their morning peak. p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~2.3s. sample request id: req-0a1b2c. anyone oncall?

carmen: i'm oncall. looking at gateway logs now. seeing a cluster of "upstream response timeout" (504) around 10:03-10:10 UTC. tenant qps peaked ~1.2k. :eyes:

mike: noted. do we know candidate list sizes? rerank has token/item limits; big candidate lists can blow up batch formation.

elaine: customer (ACME Retail) says they started sending 100 candidates per call (was 20 before) and ramped qps 4x overnight. opened ticket CS-4567 and added them here.

carmen: quick repro curl they shared:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/rerank \
 -d '{"query":"price of cloud GPUs","candidates":["...100 items..."]}'
```
we're seeing long server-side queue times; gateway retries then surfaces 502s.

mike: runtime metrics show worker backlog spiked, batch formation latency jumped, kernel execution stretched. it looks like continuous batching heuristics formed very large batches -> exceeded per-request timeout. suspect batching window increase in recent runtime.

ops: temporary mitigation applied: tenant throttle to 300 qps + enabled model fallback to smaller quantized variant for that tenant. should drop pressure while we triage.

support-bot: Ticket CS-4567 updated: applied tenant throttle + model fallback @ 2025-11-09T10:22:00Z.

julia: customer accepted the temporary throttle but wants root cause & permanent fix. also asking for repro steps and SLA impact estimate.

mike: proposed plan:
1) lower max_batch_size for rerank route
2) enforce candidate cap: default 50, hard cap 100
3) add per-tenant concurrency queue to isolate noisy neighbors
4) tweak batch timeout heuristics to avoid giant batches under high qps
I'll open an RFC/PR for the changes.

carmen: for faster mitigation i can adjust configs: set batch_timeout_ms 8->4ms and lower max_batch_tokens for rerank pools. will test on canary.

sam: any sign this is a model/kernel regression vs request pattern? any recent deploys?

deploy-bot: deploy rtx-serving v1.14.3 rolled out to canary @ 2025-11-09T09:58:14Z.

mike: v1.14.3 included a batching tweak that increases batch window under lower QPS to improve throughput. under high QPS + large candidate lists that tweak can cause huge batches. I recommend reverting v1.14.3 for high-qps pools.

elaine: customer asked for a repro script so they can validate after changes. carmen can we capture a minimal repro (qps + candidate size) and upload traces?

carmen: will run controlled load: ab-style hitting 600 qps with 60 candidates each, capture backend traces, and attach logs + X-Request-IDs. i'll paste the script here when ready.

mike: also adding a robust fallback: if batch formation time > X ms, split into smaller sub-batches instead of forming a single giant batch. that should prevent single-request timeouts.

ops: rolling back v1.14.3 from two high-qps pools now. ETA ~15m. monitoring for 502/504 drop.

support-bot: CS-4567 update: rollback started @ 2025-11-09T10:34:12Z. Customer notified.

julia: thanks — i'll update ACME with ETA, mitigation steps, and that we're working on config + code fixes.

sam: good. once carmen posts repro + traces we'll run postmortem and adjust SLO/alerts for rerank p95 and noisy-tenant detection.

(attachments planned: gateway log snippets, one sample X-Request-ID trace, proposed PR link when opened)
